text:
sasha: quick summary of today's micro-bench sweep for reranker/embedding across regions. ran CPU fallback + GPU on p4/p8 equivalents, dims [64,128,256], batch sizes [1,4,16,64].
aj: nice. did you include the proxying overhead for cross-region calls?
sasha: yes — measured local vs proxied rerank (us->eu, us->apac). proxy adds ~6-12ms p95 depending on batch.
kevin: raw numbers from the CSV: p4: dim256 batch16 throughput=980 qps, p8: batch16=3400 qps. cpu (c6i): dim256 batch16=220 qps. latency tail: p4 p95=18ms, p8 p95=9ms, cpu p95=120ms.
aj: interesting — dim scaling looks sublinear on GPU beyond 128 for latency. any kernel differences?
sasha: yes. we tested two kernel paths: fast-kv (blocks fused) vs baseline. fast-kv wins at dim<=128; at dim>=256 kernel scheduling overhead makes batching + persistent kv better.
kevin: quant note: int8 quant gave 1.8x throughput on p4 but increased p95 by ~10% on rerank due to extra dequantization steps.
bench-bot: dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.local/runs/1857654321 (csv: s3://bench/rerank/1857654321.csv)
sasha: capacity-sizing quick take: for EU region serving 99th pct latency SLO 50ms, dim128 batch4 on p4 equiv needs ~18 instances to handle 10k qps. p8 equiv ~6 instances. cpu-only would need ~60 nodes.
aj: did you try KV prefix caching for repeated queries?
sasha: yes — prefix cache reduces per-token by ~30% for rerank warm-starts, greatly helps small-batch latency. we should include caching in default policy for canary.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled: rerank-cache-policy v2 -> eu-dedicated pool at 2025-11-12T16:00Z :thumbsup:
kevin: follow-ups: 1) run dim512 quick sweep on p8 with batch1/4, 2) measure apac proxy p95 during business hours, 3) add kernel flamegraph for the slow path.
sasha: agreed. i'll queue the jobs and ping when results land. thanks! :raised_hands:
